chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: His own long drum solos with stick tricks
summary: Crawford describes drum solos of ten or fifteen minutes with stick twirling that he worked out, though early on he only kept time.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yes, I used to do a solo, drum solo on numbers like -- like Caravan and other numbers like that, but I had some worked out, hopping from Joe Jones to Big Sid, people like that. I had some worked out, and it was very interesting to see, because I had my wheels turning on my fingers also, you know, the drumsticks, throwing them in the air, catching them this way, behind me, and I had me a little act going.
Yeah, I had a little act going, so.
How long did you usually play the solos?
Oh, about -- say about 15 minutes or
ten minutes on. Oh, I had it worked out.
Oh, you played long solos then?
Yeah, just let me alone. Let me get up there and play my thing.
Now, when you played the long solos is when you were using all of the -- all of the extra equipments and --
Yeah, and when I got out of Lunsford's band, I still played pretty long solos, which was very interesting.
Now, you said before, didn't you, that you didn't -- that when you first came to New York, you didn't really like to play -- you didn't play solos (inaudible).
You couldn't play them when you first got to New York?
Yeah, because I had to work something out myself. I just sat back and kept time, that's all.
